prompt:
I need the front end for Packroom. An in-house packaging artwork hub built for the global packaging design department of a multinational snack and confectionery company, holding the approved dielines, artwork files and regulatory text for every pack the company sells in every market.

Who's using it: Marisol Achebe, a senior packaging designer who moved two weeks ago from the company's beverage division to the snacks packaging team in its regional design center. She knows packaging production well but does not yet know how the snacks brands, product lines and markets are arranged, or what the team's naming and versioning habits are.

What they're doing right now: A printer in Poland has asked for the current approved artwork for the 150 g Crunchwell Paprika pouch for the Central Europe market, due by end of day. Searching found three files with similar names, and she has ended up in a market folder for Czechia, not knowing whether Poland sits under it, next to it or somewhere else. She needs to work out where she is in the brand > product line > pack format > market > artwork version structure, step back to the right level, go across to the Polish market entry, and confirm which version is approved and which is a superseded draft. Then she has to find the related dieline and the Polish-language ingredient panel text, which are stored in other parts of the hub, and get back to the artwork afterwards.

What's in the system at this point: 14 brands (e.g., Crunchwell, Halvi, Pebbleton, Mornbrook) with 212 product lines and 1,860 active SKUs. Crunchwell has 9 product lines; Crunchwell Paprika comes in 4 pack formats (40 g, 90 g, 150 g pouch, 6×25 g multipack). The 150 g pouch has 11 market entries grouped by region (Central Europe: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary; the Czech and Slovak packs are a shared bilingual artwork). Each market entry has artwork versions (Polish 150 g: v4 approved 2026-09-03 by regulatory reviewer K. Nowak, v5 in review with a new recycling mark, v3 superseded), a linked dieline (DL-P150-07, shared across 6 markets), a regulatory text block per language, a barcode spec and a printer contact (Drukpol, Łódź). Departmental sections apart from the brand structure: dieline library (340 dielines), shared assets (logos, legal marks, recycling icons), regulatory text library by country, team guidelines, and Marisol's 23 recently viewed items.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
